name: h1024_pilot
_comment: Written 2026-11-12 before it ran. Question: does a wider net (1024 hidden units instead of 512) reach a lower loss on unseen rows with the SAME data and the SAME recipe? Everything equals h512/train/plans/scratch_wd.json (random initialisation, Adam, batch 8192, peak lr 5e-4, 500 warm-up steps, cosine to 5 % per stage, alpha 0.25, natural sampling, decoupled weight decay 0.3 on w1, the same stage ends) except cfg_override hidden 1024 and fewer periodic checkpoints (disk). Compare at equal presentations with the 512 run: 0.014126 at 1.0B, 0.014055 at 2.0B, 0.013968 at 4.0B, 0.013916 at 7.4B, 0.013882 at 10.0B on select_2m. This is a pilot on the selection set only: no candidate is taken from it without a new declaration, and it is never scored on a test set.
